_doc: ledger 0097 round 5, owed item 2: the north loop's two blue / yellow stripes, which NAIP's z18 photo cannot resolve, read off the 2018 lidar's INTENSITY. Every 0.5 m of the north loop's own s (+-1 m along): the first bright return outward from the lane (the inner side of the first paint). Either side of a stripe that is the white edge line; along the stripe it stands ~0.8 m further in: the stripe's inner side. o / in_m are metres past the north loop's built lane edge (source/full/connectors.full.json's widths, kerbs.lm.json's convention, - = inside); the _photo_frame values take off the lidar's measured shift against the 2023 photo (carried_edges.json registration). s0_s1 is the stripe's core (STRIPE_MIN_M inside the edge line), s0_s1_tapered its ends (TAPER_MIN_M inside), each +-1 m (the stations' window). The lidar is 2018; round 4's eye spans are the 2023 photo's.

source.lidar: USGS 3DEP CO_Eastern_B3_2018 lidar (public domain), its EPT: https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/usgs-lidar-public/CO_Eastern_B3_2018/ept.json
source.returns: every class but noise (7, 18); one flight line over all five spots: [1141]
source.frame: the track frame: E, N metres about data/centerline.local.json's origin, lon / lat through scripts.geometry.projection._meters_per_degree (round 4's mapping); 3857 -> lon / lat by pyproj
source.lines: the West lap as built (data/centerline.local.json + widths); the north loop's own line (source/full/connectors.full.json + widths: 'own s', the s of round 4's kerbs and stripes); OSM's line as measure_north.py builds it ('row s', north_loop.json's rows, whose left_m / right_m are metres off it)
source.script: hp_r5_lidar.py beside this file (plan / fetch / extract / measure)

params._doc: every one [invented] reader tuning; the returns are the measurement

stripe372.out_m_why: not measured: the paint (intensity p25/p50/p75 in stripe_band) and what lies past it read alike (beside_the_stripe); the lidar cannot place the stripe's outer side
stripe372.width_how: DERIVED: the stripe's inner side to the asphalt's end, where the asphalt's end is the edge line's inner side either side less the registration's c (the lidar's first bright against NAIP's edge); true if the paint runs to the asphalt's end, as the 2023 photo shows
